answer.rationale:
Two of the three current problems are internal funnel decay (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%), and only one is competitive. The competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the emotionally obvious move, but memory_73 is explicit that while it lifts acquisition and revenue it materially damaged 30-day retention and should NOT be generalized as a growth strategy. Given the stated objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, spending the single non-carrying slot on a tactic already known to trade retention for headline numbers is the wrong bet; I decline to reinterpret that warning just because the situation now feels urgent.

Among the funnel options, simplify_onboarding is the best-supported lever: memory_86 (day 52, most recent onboarding evidence) ties shortened onboarding directly to completion rate and time-to-value, which is precisely the metric that is declining, and it plausibly lifts activation downstream too, giving one experiment leverage on both regressions. activation_messaging (memory_91) is a reasonable second choice but addresses only the narrower symptom. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is real but aimed at a segment that is not where the bleeding is.

I am spending verification on the two memories my action actually rests on rather than on the one I am declining. memory_86 needs checking because its claim is the broadest ('across self-serve accounts') and I need to know whether that generalization was measured or inferred, and over what horizon — completion-rate lifts can be an artifact of moving friction later rather than removing it. memory_31 needs checking because it is the oldest here (day 12) and specifies a concrete mechanism, cutting required signup fields; I need the original record to see which fields were cut and whether qualification/routing data was among them.

Downstream value risk: stripping signup or onboarding fields can quietly degrade lead qualification and mis-route enterprise prospects away from the sales-assisted path that memory_44 shows produces better pipeline quality. That means a naive 'remove more fields' version of this test could raise completion while lowering qualified revenue — exactly the metric I am optimizing. So the design must keep segmentation/routing fields intact, and I will instrument qualified-pipeline quality and 30-day retention alongside completion, not just the top-line completion lift.

Uncertainty preserved: all six inherited claims are consolidated summaries with sources archived, so their effect sizes, durations, and populations are not directly visible to me. Standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout, because the evidence is secondhand and the two funnel declines could share an unobserved common cause (e.g. a traffic-mix shift) that no onboarding change would fix — an outcome the experiment should be able to reveal rather than mask.
